versions.changelog:
**Summary:**  
This update introduces flexible coverage requirements based on topic scope and migrates the wiki-creator integration to an internal scripts-based solution.

- Supports two review modes: whole-field (all six H-layers) or single subfield (flexible coverage per focus), with detection and user confirmation.
- Adjusts search thresholds—now mode-dependent, focusing only on relevant layers for subfield reviews.
- Clarifies "saturation" as the legitimate stopping point for further paper searches and distinguishes this from rigid round-count requirements.
- Replaces all external wiki-creator references and paths with new in-project scripts and revised documentation.
- Updates and relocates documentation, assets, and script files to reflect the new architecture and workflow.
- Removes the old `wiki-creator` component and deepens integration of the built-in scripts, supporting both clean creation and controlled incremental updates.

- Added an internal wiki-creator component for optional local wiki化, replacing the previous external dependency.
- New "wiki 化" workflow: wiki write actions require explicit user confirmation and detailed stepwise disclosure before execution.
- Updated documentation to reflect path restrictions—wiki output is now confined to a project-specific .wiki-creator directory (never home/global paths).
- Integrated scripts, templates, and references for structured wiki page creation, linting, and index building.
- Removed outdated skill-card.md and revised SKILL.md to clarify new confirmation, execution, and output rules for wiki integration.

- Initial release of the "agentic-ai-research" skill for searching and reviewing top conference and journal papers on Agentic AI.
- Implements a structured multi-stage literature search process using the H=(E,T,C,S,L,V)+P framework, with strict coverage, retrieval, and reporting rules.
- Outputs a human-readable literature review (.md) following a clear template, with categorical coverage, readable summaries, and transparent disclosure of retrieval steps.
- Requires rigorous, multi-round WebSearch-based retrieval (no APIs or pdf extraction), full coverage across six dimensions, and explicit logging of the search process.
- Integrates with llm-wiki to convert literature reviews into wiki pages after completion.
